blockers.claim: S14 Mission Detail (in-scope, not on the defer line) ships all required design-parity elements this batch.
blockers.evidence: architecture-plan.md §4.3 builds only 2 of the 5 accordions the scope authority requires: 'accordions read-only/collapsed (ALL ACTIONS / PROGRESS = TrendChart); other accordions deferred-ghost.' But scope-hifi-today-missions.md §8 ('Verification Checklist (BIOS-004 Entry Gate)') explicitly states: '- [ ] S14: Five expandable accordions: ALL ACTIONS / MILESTONES / CIA REASONING / CROSS-DOMAIN / PROGRESS OVER TIME'. Unlike every other scope cut in this plan (S41/S45/S61/S73/S93, ConstellationRadar), this one has no ADR, no Section-8 Open-Questions flag, and no mention in the Executive Summary's defer line — it is buried as a single clause in a composition-table cell. As written, the batch cannot pass the exit gate defined by its own cited source of truth for an in-scope screen.
blockers.fix: Either (a) add MILESTONES/CIA REASONING/CROSS-DOMAIN LINKS to the S14 packet scope (accepting the cap tradeoff it displaces), or (b) add this as an explicit ADR/Open-Question with the same decided-with-flag treatment given to ConstellationRadar, and amend or waive the scope-hifi §8 checklist line for S14 accordingly so close-batch verification isn't silently failing its own gate.

majors.claim: ADR-5 states new root Stack.Screen routes this batch are 'life-areas, fitness, data-controls, + new mission-detail/create/journal/celebration.'

ADR-5's route list is internally inconsistent with the rest of the plan, and the S13 TopBar 'journal glyph' (scope-hifi §3, S13 composition) has no stated destination this batch given the contradiction.

majors.claim: ADR-8 and the Test Plan (§6) verify the EAS submission via 'a local-JWT ASC script (scripts/verify-asc-state.sh, ES256 from the gitignored .p8)' as if it is an existing, ready tool.
majors.evidence: scope-release.md §5 states plainly: 'Status: Pattern documented, but no standalone implementation found' and lists `./scripts/verify-asc-state.sh # (not found)`. Section 5's packet decomposition (the batch's actual task list, waves 0-4) assigns no owner or wave to creating this script — it appears nowhere in the Wave/Packet table.
majors.fix: Add a lander task (Wave 0 or Wave-EAS) to author scripts/verify-asc-state.sh before ADR-8 is executed, or explicitly fall back to the scope-release.md-documented workaround (manual expo.dev/ASC-portal check) and say so in ADR-8.

majors.claim: Executive Summary / ADR-7: 'react-native-svg / expo-haptics / expo-linear-gradient are all Expo-Go-compatible SDK-57 modules (present in node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json) — the "dev build needed" claim is wrong.'
majors.evidence: bundledNativeModules.json lists every SDK-57-compatible package for `expo install` version resolution across ALL Expo apps (managed or bare) — it is not a list of modules compiled into the official App Store Expo Go client, which is a much narrower, curated native-module set. Separately, this project already ships via a **custom dev client**: `expo-dev-client` is a direct dependency, and eas.json's `development`/`simulator` profiles set `developmentClient: true`. There is no evidence anywhere in the repo that the team tests via the literal Expo Go app. ADR-8 itself immediately requires a 'dev-client simulator build' for smoke testing, which contradicts the 'Expo-Go-compatible ... dev build needed claim is wrong' framing in the same document — the scout's practical conclusion (a dev build/EAS build is needed) was actually correct; only the terminology used to rebut it is wrong.
majors.fix: Reword ADR-7/Exec-Summary to say these packages are confirmed present at the pinned SDK-57 version and already compiled into the project's existing custom dev-client/EAS-build pipeline (not 'Expo-Go-compatible', which is a different and moot claim given this project doesn't use the Expo Go app).

majors.claim: Packet table (§5): Wave 4a 'Today recompose' lists dependencies as only '1*, 2*'.
majors.evidence: ADR-3 states Today's 'Pinned missions ×2' section is sourced from `useMissions()` (§4.1 row 6), and Wave 3a is precisely the packet that rewrites the missions adapter to 6 tiers that `useMissions()` returns. 4a's declared 'Depends on' column omits 3a. Wave-number ordering (0→1→2→3→4) happens to sequence this correctly in practice, but the explicit per-packet dependency annotation — the mechanism this document uses elsewhere to prevent file-conflict/readiness mistakes — is incomplete for a worker auditing 4a's prerequisites in isolation.
majors.fix: Add '3a' to Wave 4a's Depends-on column for documentation completeness/audit correctness.

minors.claim: ADR-5 imports the JS Tabs navigator via `import { Tabs } from 'expo-router'`.
minors.evidence: node_modules/expo-router/build/exports.js:111 marks this export `@deprecated Use import { Tabs } from 'expo-router/js-tabs' instead.` Both paths resolve to the identical `./build/layouts/Tabs` module (confirmed by reading node_modules/expo-router/js-tabs.js), so this is functionally correct today but will emit a deprecation warning and is a future-removal risk.
minors.fix: Cite `expo-router/js-tabs` as the import path in the GlassNavBar packet contract instead of the deprecated top-level `expo-router` export.

minors.claim: GlassNavBar component contract (§3) implements the canon spec for the bottom nav.
minors.evidence: COMPONENT-CATALOG reference (scope-hifi §5) describes GlassNavBar as a 'floating bottom pill (4 tabs...)'. The plan's contract and ADR-5 only specify safe-area bottom padding, 44px targets, and glass material — not the floating/pill form factor (vs. a full-width edge-to-edge bar), leaving that dimension of design fidelity unresolved.
minors.fix: Add explicit pill/floating dimensions (margin, radius, width) to the GlassNavBar contract so the GLM packet doesn't default to a full-width bar.

minors.claim: S42 composition map (§4.5): 'GlassStatCard(flush) "+{delta} XP · you earned it"'.

The plan's composition-map cell collapses these into one concatenated string inside a single component slot, which risks the GLM packet building a fused label rather than the spec's three-part visual structure.
minors.fix: Expand the S42 packet contract to explicitly preserve Display + sub-copy + ChipProvenance as separate elements, matching the hi-fi spec's anatomy.
